semitone_anchor.description: The central semitone interval is always solmized as mi-fa regardless of absolute pitch.

step_directions.purpose: Reflecting melodic contour and maintaining a reserve of solmization syllables for continued movement.

mutation_logic.trigger: Occurs when melody exceeds the six steps of the active hexachord or when non-normative semitone shifts occur.
mutation_logic.technique: Rename the pitch at the transition boundary to align with the syllables of the overlapping hexachord (typically renaming a pitch to fa at a relative flat or new clef).

relative_flat.function: Relatively forces the marked sound to be solmized as fa (upper sound of the semitone).

relative_clef_C.function: Fixes the upper semitonic sound (fa) strictly on the lines of the staff.

relative_clef_Cb.function: Fixes the upper semitonic sound (fa) strictly in the spaces of the staff.

pauk.function: Phrase or line concluding cadence formula.

execution.cadence_variation: Different transcriptions and melodic executions for each of the Eight Tones (Octoechos).
execution.character: Melodically complex and highly ornamental, requiring precise vocal articulation to prevent discord during choral unison.

pauk.scholarly_context: Found in early modern primers and fitniki (e.g., Sol. 690/774, Sof. 461) where names like 'great' (bolshoy) in relation to pauk designate the need to select a specific, complex chant variant.

suprasl.character: Western Belarusian / Kyivan Caves Lavra monastic singing branch.

liturgical_features.obikhod_demesne: Monastic demesne singing concentrated in the Obikhod section.
liturgical_features.triodion_balkan: Greek-Balkan kalophonic influences in the Triodion section.
liturgical_features.chant_duration: Chants are exceptionally prolonged compared to standard 17th-century Kyivan Notation (e.g. Psalm 103 selected verses 15 and 24).
liturgical_features.through_composed: Psalm 103 ('Introductory Psalm') and 'Blessed is the Man' are through-composed without verse/word repetitions.
liturgical_features.modal_mutation: High density of relative flat and clef shifts in Tones 2, 5, 6, and 8 to represent local microtonal/modal adjustments.

notated_variants.polyeleos: Great Polyeleos 'Praise, O servants of the Lord' marked as Multanian chant.
notated_variants.kondak: Earliest record of Kyivan Notation for the Kondak 'Vozbrannoy Voyevode' (unnamed).

manyava_skete.character: Ciscarpathian monastic singing branch, Job Knyahynytsky tradition.

liturgical_features.liturgy_canon: Eucharistic Canon of St. Basil the Great in the Liturgy section is named 'Skete' or left unnamed (e.g. 'Peace be upon you').
liturgical_features.service_sequence: Strict daily cycle structure: Resurrectional Vespers and Matins, Liturgy, feast stichera, and the 9th Odes of the canons.
liturgical_features.byzantine_elements: Late Byzantine elements including papadikai, asmatikai, akolouthiai, and psaltikai techniques.

liturgical_features.bulgarian_density: High density of Bulgarian chant variants in the Sunday Octoechos.
liturgical_features.polyeleos_duality: Polyeleos 'Praise, O servants of the Lord' recorded in dual versions: 'Bulgarian' and 'Pidhirya'.

liturgical_features.ordinary_variants: Includes local Mezhyhirya versions of ordinary chants (e.g., sidalni, Gradual Antiphons, and polyeleos) showcasing regional variations of traditional Kiev-Pechersk models.

lyubachiv.character: Western Ukrainian regional diocese singing branch.

liturgical_features.triple_ordinary: Resurrectional Matins 'God is the Lord' of Tone 1 recorded in three distinct regional chants: weekday Rus', Volhynian, and Bulgarian.
liturgical_features.podobni_bulgarian: Small Bulgarian mnogomylostyvoe is preferred in the model stichera (podobni) section.
